Grand Hyatt

Staff Accommodation Platform · Dashboard design system v2 (enterprise)

The design system for the Grand Hyatt staff accommodation platform: one responsive web app used by Super Admins, Accommodation Admins, Reception, residents, maintenance, vendors and security. It takes the brand's red and its tracked, uppercase wordmark, and sets them in a clean, modern UI built from frosted glass panels over a softly lit page.

Principles

  1. Calm, like a grand hotel lobby. Generous space, few colours on screen at once, one primary action per view. Red is an accent people notice, not a fill everywhere.
  2. Glass for structure, solid for anchors. Cards, top bar and drawers are frosted glass. The sidebar is solid deep ink, so the layout always has a fixed edge.
  3. Action first. Every role home opens with what needs the user now (the Needs action queue), then today, then health KPIs.
  4. Readable whatever is behind. Glass never carries long text on its own: tables, forms and menus use glass-strong. All text meets 4.5:1 in both themes.
  5. Status is consistent. One status, one badge tone, everywhere in the app.

Content fundamentals

  • Sentence case for everything except eyebrows, table headers and the brand lockup, which are uppercase and tracked like the wordmark.
  • Buttons are verbs: "Check in", "Allocate bed", "Approve", "Trigger exit". Never "Submit" or "OK".
  • Plain, courteous, specific. Say what happened and what to do: "Building has occupants. 38 of 42 beds are occupied, so it can't be archived."
  • Codes and numbers in tabular figures (PV-V07-R2-B, 92.4%). Dates as "Wed 14 Oct", times 24-hour.
  • Address people by first name in greetings only ("Good morning, Anita"); elsewhere use full names.

Visual foundations

Colour. Grand Hyatt red #C42737, sampled from the client logo, is the brand-fill token: primary buttons, the active nav bar, the occupied segment, counts. As text on light it is brand; in dark mode brand lightens to stay legible while brand-fill keeps the true red. champagne is the quiet premium second colour for charts, the reserved state and dividers; in light mode it is a fill only (text fails contrast). Neutrals are warm (bg #F5F1F0, ink #1D1A1B), never blue-grey.

Glass. A glass surface = glass fill + backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-md)) saturate(140%) + 1px glass-border + radius-lg + shadow-glass. Glass only reads as glass over something: every page sits on bg with two blurred glow blobs (bg-glow red-tinted top right, bg-glow-2 champagne bottom left), applied by the .gh-canvas class. Never stack glass on glass; inside cards use glass-subtle rows or hairlines. Browsers without backdrop-filter fall back to the solid-enough glass-strong.

Type. Two families. Jost (display, Google Fonts) echoes the geometric, widely tracked capitals of the wordmark: used for the greeting (display, uppercase, 0.08em) and every eyebrow and table header (eyebrow, 11px, 0.16em). Inter carries the interface: h1 22, h2 15, h3 14, body 14/22, body-sm 13/20, label 13/18, kpi 28 with tabular figures. Jost stands in for the brand's proprietary typeface; swap it in tokens.json if the client supplies licensed fonts.

Space and shape. A 4px base: space-2 8 inside controls, space-4 16 card gaps, space-6 24 card padding and grid gutters, space-8 32 between sections. Corners soften with size: radius-xs 4 checkboxes, radius-sm 6 badges, radius-md 8 buttons, inputs and nav, radius-lg 12 cards, radius-xl 16 modals and the sidebar, radius-pill chips and avatars.

Elevation. Hairline-first: a 1px border does most of the work. shadow-xs on controls, shadow-glass on cards, shadow-raised on menus and modals. No coloured glows.

Status colours. success green, warning amber, danger red, info blue, each with a -soft badge background, all checked at ≥4.9:1. danger sits close to the brand red, so a danger state always carries an icon or label, never colour alone.

Data colours. Bed status everywhere: occupied brand-fill, reserved champagne, available info, blocked / maintenance ink-subtle. Charts add ink and success before any new hue.

Layout

  • Desktop: 248px solid sidebar (workspace switcher on top, user footer below) + main column; a glass top bar with global search, the site scope switcher (only for multi-site users), notifications and avatar. Main column: page header (eyebrow · greeting · one-line summary · up to two actions), four stat tiles, then a 1.6 : 1 grid of Needs action queue and side cards, then the day's table.
  • Below 900px the sidebar hides; stat tiles go two-up and the grid stacks. Resident, technician, contractor and security screens are designed phone-first with a bottom tab bar and 38px+ touch targets.
  • The sidebar shows only modules the role may open (see the Roles, Permissions & Module Map document).

Iconography

Lucide (ISC licence), drawn at 16px with a 1.75 stroke in currentColor via GH.Icon. One icon per concept, used the same way in nav, stat tiles and action rows. No emoji, no filled or duotone icons, no icon in a coloured circle without a status reason.

Logo

The supplied wordmark (assets/Logos/grand-hyatt-logo.png) goes on the sign-in page and exported reports, on white or bg only. Inside the app the sidebar carries a text lockup in the display face. A vector and a reversed version are still needed from the client.

Using this system

Load the tokens (tokens.css), then components/bundle.css (it imports Inter and Jost from Google Fonts), React 18, and components/bundle.js, which exposes window.GH: Button, Badge, Icon, GlassCard, StatTile (with sparkline and delta), ActionItem, Field, SearchField, Tabs, Breadcrumb, PageHeader, NavItem, Sidebar, DataTable (selection, toolbar, pager), OccupancyBar, Avatar, Alert. Each component's guidelines are in its README; Admin dashboard under Pages shows them assembled into the Accommodation Admin home. Themes switch with data-theme="light|dark" on the root.

Admin dashboard (assembled)

Dark theme

Components

Button

Button

Four variants on a 36px control (30px sm), 8px corners, a 1px edge and a hairline shadow.

Variant Use
primary The one main task of the view (brand red). At most one per view.
secondary Every other action: white glass, 1px border.
ghost Low-weight actions in rows, toolbars and cancel.
danger Destructive or loss actions: red text, turns red-tinted on hover.
  • Labels are verbs in sentence case: "Allocate bed", "Check in", "Trigger exit".
  • Icon-only buttons (pass icon without children) always need aria-label; use them for filter, more, export in toolbars.
  • Hide actions the user has no permission for; disabled is only for temporary states.
  • Focus: 2px page-colour gap, then a 4px red focus ring.

Badge

Badge

A compact 22px status label: 6px corners, a tinted background and a status dot. Use outline (no fill) or dot={false} for non-status tags such as stay type or property type.

Tone Use for
success Checked in, approved, resolved, ready, within SLA
info Reserved, scheduled, in progress, provisional
warning Due today, checkout due, expiring, on hold
danger Overdue, breached SLA, lost key, SOS, rejected
brand Waiting on you / needs approval
neutral Draft, archived, closed, cancelled

Every record status maps to exactly one tone, the same everywhere. Danger sits close to the brand red, so the label is always shown; colour never stands alone.

Icon

Icon

The platform uses Lucide (v0.460.0, ISC licence), a professional open-source line-icon set: 24px grid, 1.75 stroke, rounded joins, drawn in currentColor. The icons used by the platform are inlined in the bundle under short names (dashboard, building, bed, swap, check, wrench, key, box, calendar, shield, chart, file, users…).

  • 16px in buttons, nav and tables; 20px in empty states and module tiles. Never mix icon sets or add filled icons.
  • One icon per module, used the same way in nav, stat tiles and action rows.
  • Pass label when an icon stands alone without text; otherwise it is hidden from screen readers.
  • Need another icon? Pick it from lucide.dev and add it to the bundle under a short name.

GlassCard

GlassCard

The core surface: translucent glass fill with blur-md backdrop blur, a crisp 1px border, an inner top highlight (glass-border), radius-lg (12px) and the soft shadow-glass.

Slots: title + optional subtitle or eyebrow, right-aligned actions, body, optional footer (meta such as "Updated 2 min ago", pagination). divider adds a line under the header; flush removes body padding for tables and lists.

  • strong (92% opaque) for tables, forms and long text, so readability never depends on what is behind.
  • Never nest glass in glass; inside a card use hairlines or glass-subtle rows.
  • Pages sit on bg with two very soft glows (.gh-canvas) so the glass reads as glass without looking decorative.

StatTile

StatTile

One KPI: label, large tabular number with an optional unit, a delta chip, a comparison hint, and either a sparkline (for trends) or an outlined icon (for counts).

  • trend sets the arrow; good sets the colour. For KPIs where up is bad (open work orders, overdue keys) pass good={false} so the chip and sparkline turn red.
  • The hint always names the comparison or target: "vs last month", "target 95%".
  • Sparkline: the last 7–12 periods, no axes; the end point is marked.
  • Four per row on desktop, two on phone. Each tile opens the filtered list behind the number, if the user may see it.

ActionItem

ActionItem

A row in a role's Needs action queue, inside a flush GlassCard: tinted icon chip, title, one-line meta, optional urgency badge, count, and a chevron that opens the filtered list.

  • The queue is the first card on every role home; list only what this user can act on, highest risk first.
  • Tone signals urgency: danger = overdue/breached, warning = due soon, brand = waiting on you, info = upcoming.
  • Hide a row when its count is zero; show an empty state ("You're all caught up") when the queue is empty.

Field

Field

Label, 36px input, hint or error. Inputs are near-opaque glass with a 1px border, a hairline shadow, and a red 3px focus ring.

  • Labels above inputs, sentence case, no colons. Required is the default; optional fields say "(optional)".
  • Errors replace the hint, say what to fix, and set aria-invalid.
  • Masked personal data (ID numbers) shows as read-only text, never in an input.
  • SearchField is the global search in the top bar (people, beds, keys, tickets), filtered by the user's permissions, with a ⌘K / Ctrl K shortcut hint.

Tabs

Tabs

A segmented control for switching views of the same data (time range; arrivals / departures / transfers). Two to five short options, optional counts. For moving between pages, use the sidebar.

Breadcrumb

Breadcrumb

Shows where the user is in the site hierarchy or a module: Module › Site › Building › Room. Every level except the last is a link. Sits above the page title in PageHeader; hide it on role homes.

PageHeader

PageHeader

Top of every page: breadcrumb, title (h1, 22px), a one-line summary with the key counts, and at most two actions on the right (one primary).

Role homes use display (uppercase, tracked display face) for the greeting and an eyebrow with role and date instead of a breadcrumb.

NavItem

NavItem

One sidebar link: 16px icon, label, optional count. Active item: lighter fill, white label, red icon. Counts show only items waiting on this user (approvals, untriaged tickets), never totals.

Sidebar

Sidebar

The solid deep-ink navigation column, the one non-glass surface that anchors the layout: workspace switcher (GH mark, brand, product; opens the site/workspace menu), permission-filtered groups, and the signed-in user with role at the bottom.

  • Build groups from the user's permissions; never show a module the role can't open. Order follows the role navigation table in the Roles & Permissions doc.
  • Below 900px it hides; phone roles (resident, technician, security) get a bottom tab bar, admin roles a menu sheet.
  • The GH mark is a monogram placeholder; replace it with the official reversed logo once the client supplies it.

DataTable

DataTable

Record lists inside a strong, flush GlassCard: optional toolbar (search, filters, export), optional row selection, tinted header row, hairline rows, hover and selected states, and a footer with count and pagination.

  • First column identifies the record (avatar + name + department, or the bed code). Codes use tabular figures (mono).
  • Status is always a Badge; descriptive tags (stay type) use the outline badge.
  • One primary row action at most (e.g. "Check in" when it's due); everything else goes in the row's ⋯ menu.
  • Selection and bulk actions appear only for roles with that grant.
  • Masked personal data shows as "•••• 4417". On phone, rows collapse into stacked cards.

OccupancyBar

OccupancyBar

Headline occupancy, a segmented bed-status bar and a two-column legend with counts. The colour mapping is fixed everywhere: occupied = brand-fill, reserved = champagne, available = info, blocked / maintenance = ink-subtle. Segments are separated by a 2px gap and the legend always shows the numbers, so it reads without relying on colour.

Avatar

Avatar

Initials in a neutral circle with a hairline ring; brand (red) only for the signed-in user. Use the person's photo when one exists and the viewer may see it (Reception and Security verification).

Alert

Alert

Inline message: coloured icon, bold title, muted detail, optional action. Neutral glass background for info, warning and success, so a page with several alerts stays calm; danger gets a red tint because it blocks the task. Lead with what happened, then what to do.
